title: Integral point sections detect zero objects
statement: Let D be a finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], let l be prime distinct from its characteristic, and let E/Q_l be finite. Use the integral constructible category and the finite and integral section functors of [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]. Assume that the finite fibre functor is an equivalence at every positive reduction level. If K is an integral constructible complex and its integral section complex is zero, then K is zero.

source.place: Integral point sections detect zero objects; extracted from the point-fibre argument; lean/Sheaf/Paper/PointIntegralSectionsConservative.lean, pointIntegralSections_conservative

proof.text: Compare the small section-derived category and its standard large model using their exact homology comparison isomorphisms. Vanishing of integral sections thus holds in the model used by the normalized sections/reduction comparison. Derived tensor is triangulated and sends this zero section complex to zero. Apply the sections/reduction isomorphism to see that sections of every finite reduction vanish.

source.place: Integral equivalence, reduction part of step 8

proof.text: Finite fibre equivalence reflects zero. Thus each actual finite reduction of K is zero. Restricting coefficients preserves zero, and the universal property of the product makes the product of all restricted reductions zero. In the defining Roos completeness triangle for K both product vertices are zero, so its first vertex K is zero. No tensor resolution is assigned any finite amplitude in this argument.

theorem pointIntegralSections_conservative
    (D : FiniteFieldDatum.{u}) (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (hl : l ≠ D.p)
    (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra ℚ_[l] E] [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] E]
    (hf : ∀ (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n), (pointFiniteFibre D l hl E n hn).IsEquivalence)
    (K : sfIntegralConstructibleCategory l E (Spec (.of D.k)))
    (hK : IsZero ((pointFibreIntegralAmbient D l E).obj K.obj)) : IsZero K.obj
